question: Which statement best describes Partial, Required, and Readonly?
options: These operate on union types. `Exclude<U, X>` removes members of U assignable to X; `Extract<U, X>` keeps only those assignable to X; `NonNullable<T>` removes null and undefined from T. They're built on conditional types and are handy for narrowing unions.

These three remap a type's properties' modifiers. `Partial<T>` makes every property optional (great for update/patch payloads). `Required<T>` makes every property required (removing all `?`). `Readonly<T>` makes every property immutable. They're mapped types over keyof T under the hood.

These select a subset of properties. `Pick<T, K>` keeps only the keys in K (K extends keyof T). `Omit<T, K>` is the inverse — every property except K. Use Pick to build a narrow view of a type and Omit to strip fields (like removing a password before returning a user).

`Record<K, V>` builds an object type whose keys are K (a union of string/number/symbol literals) and whose values are all V. It's the idiomatic way to type dictionaries, lookup maps, and config objects keyed by a known set of names.
